easy.def: A big musical instrument with black and white keys.
examples: I play the piano.
The piano is in the living room.
She sat at the piano.

more.def: A large musical instrument with black and white keys that make sounds when you press them.
examples: She practices the piano for twenty minutes every day.
The piano player pressed the keys softly.
A grand piano filled the center of the stage.

easy.def: To choose one.
examples: Pick a card.
She picked the red one.
I will pick a book.

more.def: To choose one thing or person from a group.
examples: Pick any book from the shelf that you like.
The coach picked her to be team captain.
I picked the biggest pumpkin in the patch.

easy.def: To take fruit or flowers from a plant.
examples: We pick apples.
She picked a flower.
I pick berries.

more.def: To pull fruit, flowers, or leaves off a plant.
examples: We picked strawberries at the farm on Saturday.
She picked a bunch of daisies for her mother.
The farmers pick the apples in the fall.

easy.def: A drawing, a painting or a photo.
examples: I drew a picture of my dog.
There is a picture on the wall.
Mom took a picture of us.

more.def: A drawing, painting or photograph that shows how something looks.
examples: She painted a picture of the mountains.
Dad took a picture of us at the beach.
A picture of a dragon is on the book's cover.

easy.def: To see something in your mind.
examples: Picture a big red balloon.
I can picture my house.
Can you picture the beach?

more.def: To form an image of something in your mind.
examples: Close your eyes and picture a quiet forest.
He pictured himself winning the race.
I can picture the whole room, with the red couch.

easy.def: A baked treat with a crust and filling.
examples: I ate apple pie.
We bake a pie.
The pie is hot.

more.def: A baked food with a pastry crust and a sweet or salty filling.
examples: Grandma baked an apple pie.
We had pumpkin pie after dinner.
The pie cooled on the windowsill.

easy.def: A part of something bigger.
examples: I ate a piece of pie.
A piece fell off the toy.
Give me a piece of paper.

more.def: A part that has been cut, broken or taken from a whole thing.
examples: She cut the cake into twelve equal pieces.
One piece of the puzzle was missing.
He tore a piece of tape off the roll.

easy.def: One work of music, writing or art.
examples: She played a piece on the piano.
That piece of music is slow.
The art show has a piece by every child.

more.def: A single work of music, writing or art.
examples: The orchestra played a lovely piece by a famous composer.
The student read a short piece of her writing to the class.
He painted a piece for the school gallery.

easy.def: A farm animal with a curly tail.
examples: The pig rolled in mud.
Pigs oink.
A pig lives on the farm.

more.def: A farm animal with a round body, short legs, a curly tail and a flat nose.
examples: The pig rolled in the mud to keep cool.
Farmers raise pigs for food.
A pig can run faster than you might think.

easy.def: A lot of things on top of each other.
examples: I made a pile of leaves.
A pile of books is on the desk.
The pile of laundry is big.

more.def: A group of things lying one on top of another.
examples: The kids jumped into a pile of leaves.
A pile of books sat on the desk.
She put the dirty clothes in a pile.

easy.def: To put things on top of each other.
examples: Pile the books on the table.
She piled the toys.
Snow piled up.

more.def: To make a heap of things.
examples: He piled the wood next to the fireplace.
Snow piled up against the door.
She piled all the cushions on the floor.

easy.def: A small tablet of medicine.
examples: He took a pill.
The pill is small.
Swallow the pill with water.

more.def: A small, hard piece of medicine that you swallow.
examples: He took a pill with a glass of water.
The pill helped stop her headache.
The doctor gave me a pill for my cough.

easy.def: A soft cushion for your head in bed.
examples: I sleep on a pillow.
The pillow is soft.
I hugged my pillow.

more.def: A soft bag filled with feathers or foam that you rest your head on.
examples: I put my head on a soft pillow.
The kids had a pillow fight.
She hugged her pillow and fell asleep.

easy.def: A person who flies a plane.
examples: The pilot flew the plane.
My uncle is a pilot.
The pilot said hello.

more.def: A person who flies an airplane or other aircraft.
examples: The pilot announced the weather.
My uncle is a pilot for an airline.
The pilot landed the plane safely.

easy.def: A thin, short piece of metal with a sharp point.
examples: Mom used a pin to hold the cloth.
I found a pin on the floor.
Put a pin in the map.

more.def: A small, thin piece of metal with a sharp point, used to hold things together.
examples: The tailor held the cloth with a pin.
She put a pin in the map to show where we went.
A pin on the corkboard held up the notice.

easy.def: To stick something on a wall.
examples: She pinned the paper to the board.
I pin my name tag on.
Pin the card to the wall.

more.def: To fasten something in place using a small, sharp piece of metal.
examples: The teacher pinned our drawings to the board.
He pinned a ribbon on his shirt.
Mom pinned up the hem of my pants.

easy.def: Light red.
examples: The flower is pink.
She wears a pink dress.
A pink balloon.

more.def: Having a light red color, like cotton candy.
examples: The sunset turned the sky pink.
She wore a pink ribbon in her hair.
The pink flowers bloomed in spring.

easy.def: The color light red.
examples: Pink is my favorite color.
Mix red and white for pink.
The walls are painted pink.

more.def: A light red color made by mixing red and white.
examples: Mix red and white to make pink.
The sky glowed in shades of pink.
Pink is a soft color.

easy.def: A tube that water or gas moves through.
examples: Water runs through the pipe.
The pipe is leaking.
A pipe is under the sink.

more.def: A long, hollow tube that carries water, gas or other things from one place to another.
examples: The plumber fixed the broken pipe under the sink.
Pipes bring clean water to every house in town.
A frozen pipe burst in the cold winter.

easy.def: A robber who sails the sea in a ship.
examples: The pirate had a patch on his eye.
Pirates hide treasure.
I dressed as a pirate.

more.def: A person who sails on the sea and steals from other ships, in stories and in the past.
examples: The pirate buried his treasure on the island.
Pirates sailed the seas in tall ships.
The pirate in the story had a parrot on his shoulder.

easy.def: A big hole in the ground.
examples: We dug a pit.
The pit is deep.
They fell into the pit.

more.def: A large hole in the ground.
examples: We dug a pit for the campfire.
The workers dug a deep pit.
A cat fell into the muddy pit.

easy.def: The hard seed in a fruit like a peach.
examples: I spit out the pit.
The cherry has a pit.
The peach pit is hard.

more.def: The large, hard seed in the middle of some fruits, such as a peach or cherry.
examples: Be careful, there is a pit in the cherry.
He planted a peach pit in the garden.
The olive has a small pit.

easy.def: To throw a ball to the batter.
examples: He will pitch the ball.
The pitcher pitched fast.
She pitched the ball.

more.def: To throw the ball in baseball toward the batter.
examples: He pitched the ball right over the plate.
The coach pitched to each player during practice.
She pitched all nine innings.

easy.def: To set up a tent.
examples: We pitch the tent.
They pitched camp by the lake.
Dad pitched our tent.

more.def: To put up a tent and fix it in place.
examples: We pitched our tent beside the river.
They pitched camp at the edge of the woods.
Dad pitched the tent before it got dark.

easy.def: How high or low a sound is.
examples: The bird sang at a high pitch.
Her voice has a low pitch.
The pitch of the note went up.

more.def: How high or low a musical note or sound is.
examples: A violin plays a high pitch, and a tuba a low one.
The pitch of her voice rose when she got excited.
The tuner checks the pitch of each piano string.

easy.def: A sad feeling for someone who is having a hard time.
examples: I felt pity for the lost puppy.
She felt pity for him.
The story filled me with pity.

more.def: A feeling of sorrow for someone who is in trouble or pain.
examples: He felt pity for the lost kitten shivering in the rain.
She looked at the old man with pity.
The children showed pity for the hurt bird.

easy.def: Something that makes you sad or sorry.
examples: It is a pity you cannot come.
What a pity it rained!
It's a pity the game ended.

more.def: A cause for sadness or disappointment.
examples: It is a pity that you missed the show.
What a pity the picnic was canceled.
It would be a pity to waste this good food.

easy.def: A round, flat bread with cheese and tomato.
examples: I love pizza.
We ate pizza for dinner.
The pizza is hot.

more.def: A flat, round bread baked with tomato sauce, cheese and other toppings.
examples: We ordered a pizza with cheese.
Pizza is baked in a hot oven.
She added mushrooms to her pizza.
